finding.claim: Unauthenticated full-read SSRF. The POST parameter 'feed' goes straight into file_get_contents(), which accepts http(s)://, ftp://, file://, php://, and similar wrappers. The response size is echoed back. This lets an attacker probe internal hosts and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and distinguish live from dead targets by the length.

trace.note: Handler is entered on any POST that has 'feed'. No auth check.
The raw user value is passed to file_get_contents(), which makes the outbound request or reads the local file.
strlen($xml) is echoed back, giving a response-size oracle. The content itself is not returned.

finding.guards_checked: There is no require_admin() call on this path (it is only defined at lines 4-9 and used on the webhook path). There is no scheme allowlist, host allowlist, DNS or IP resolution check, or private/link-local range blocklist. Redirects are followed by default. No other validation exists.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen($xml). The only auth check, require_admin() at lines 4-9, is called only at line 18 on the webhook path. Nothing validates the scheme or host. The "full-read" label overstates it: only the length is returned, so this is a size-oracle SSRF, as the trace's own note says.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF. The 'set_webhook' POST parameter is passed to curl_init() and the request is executed immediately. curl accepts http, https, gopher, file, ftp, dict and other protocols, since CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is not restricted. A compromised or malicious admin can reach internal services and cloud metadata. The response is not returned, so it is blind SSRF.
finding.sink: curl_exec($ch) on a handle created with curl_init($hook) at import.php:20-22

trace.note: Handler is entered when 'set_webhook' is present.
$hook is assigned the raw user value.
curl_exec() sends the request. The URL is only stored in the handle and nothing is validated first.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is require_admin() (session is_admin), so exploitation needs an admin session or a session-fixation or privilege-escalation bug. There is no scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP blocking, and no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS or CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS restriction. Severity is lower than SSRF-1 because of the auth gate and the blind response.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 (session is_admin check, exits 403); no URL, scheme or host validation
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so the source is admin-only and not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker.
